newsitem.title: INDIA: India seizes biggest post-reform gold haul.
newsitem.headline: India seizes biggest post-reform gold haul.

text.p: India's revenue intelligence officials said on Thursday they had seized some 62 kgs (140.8 lbs) of smuggled gold, their biggest haul of the contraband metal since India allowed official imports of gold in 1992.
Officials valued the haul at 31 million rupees (US$885,700).
A.K. Pande, head of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), told reporters that Wednesday's seizure near the land border with Nepal would substantially boost this year's find.
Since the 1992 reforms, designed partly to discourage smuggling, the average annual recovery of illegal imports has been around one tonne.
There were no immediate figures for seizures before the reforms, but Pande said: "After the new scheme was introduced on the import of gold, this is the biggest seizure."
"Given the fact this is the wedding and festive season, gold imports usually go up. But its smuggling is a bit puzzling," Pande said.
He added: "The official import this year till October was about 210 tonnes. That's between two-thirds to three-fourths of national consumption."
Pande said he expected the full year total for official imports to exceed 240 tonnes.
Other estimates put India's annual official and non-official consumption as high as 500 tonnes, and that it spends $3.4 billion on imports.
Before the changes to the law in 1992, virtually all the gold that India consumed was smuggled.

The smuggling of gold, silver and durable goods helped fuel the nation's huge black market economy, which the government estimates makes up between 20 percent and 50 percent of India's gross domestic product.
